A styling toolkit that provides ready-made style classes.
A named value, such as ink, that many rules can reuse. It is written with a double dash in front of the name.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Loads the Tailwind styling base
sections.what: Pulls in the Tailwind base, component and utility styles. The next colour rule starts here.
sections.why: Other pages rely on the ready-made classes this brings in.

sections.name: [data-mode='calm']
sections.title: Calm light colour set
sections.what: Defines the light, quiet colour set used by default, with a near-white background, dark text and grey tones for secondary text and lines. It also sets the body and display fonts and the page side margin.
sections.why: Gives the default editorial look. Reason for the exact values is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Colour values are plain numbers rather than colour names, so any edit must keep that format.

sections.name: .force-dark
sections.title: Dark terminal colour set
sections.what: Defines the dark, black-terminal colour set used in nerd mode and by any page that forces dark. Its selector list starts on the line before, so it also covers nerd mode.
sections.why: Gives a second, high-contrast look. Reason for the exact values is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: These values draw text and lines across the site in nerd mode, so a mistake shows up in many places.

sections.name: [data-mode='nerd']
sections.title: Nerd mode monospace fonts
sections.what: In nerd mode, switches body and display text to a monospace font, where every letter has the same width, and tightens the letter spacing.
sections.why: Likely reason: matches the black terminal look.
sections.watch_out: The fonts must be loaded by the site, otherwise the browser falls back to a generic monospace font.

sections.name: .force-dark
sections.title: Forced dark background
sections.what: Makes any element with the force-dark class show the dark background and light text.
sections.why: Lets a page stay dark whichever mode the visitor picked.
sections.watch_out: Pages with this class ignore the calm colours, so their text colours must come from the dark set.

sections.name: html
sections.title: Page background and text colour
sections.what: Sets the page background and text colour from the current mode, makes jumps to anchors scroll smoothly, and stops phones from resizing text on their own.
sections.why: Keeps the whole page in the chosen mode, including areas outside the main content.
sections.watch_out: Smooth scrolling is switched off for visitors who ask for less motion, so nothing essential should depend on it.

sections.name: body
sections.title: Body text and sideways scroll
sections.what: Applies the body font, smooths text rendering, sets background and text colours, fades colour changes over about a third of a second, and hides any sideways overflow.
sections.why: Gives every page one font and a smooth mode switch. Likely reason for hiding overflow: stops layouts sliding sideways on phones.
sections.watch_out: Hiding overflow can silently cut off wide content rather than fixing the layout that made it too wide.

sections.name: ::selection
sections.title: Highlight colour for selected text
sections.what: When a visitor selects text, it shows with the paper colour as its background and the ink colour as its letters.
sections.why: Keeps selected text readable in both modes.

sections.name: :focus-visible
sections.title: Keyboard focus outline
sections.what: Draws a thin light outline around whatever has keyboard focus, so people using the Tab key can see where they are.
sections.why: Keyboard users need a visible position on the page.
sections.watch_out: Removing this rule would make keyboard navigation hard to follow.

sections.name: [id]
sections.title: Anchor targets clear the nav bar
sections.what: When a link jumps to a section with an id, the page stops that section just below the fixed top bar instead of hiding it underneath.
sections.why: The top bar sits over the page, so jumps need extra space.
sections.watch_out: The space is based on the nav height value, so change the two together.

sections.name: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)  (part 1)
sections.title: Reduced motion and shared text styles
sections.what: Turns off most animation and transitions for visitors who ask for less motion. It also defines the shared text styles, such as small monospace labels and large display headings, that pages use.
sections.why: Likely reason: respects a device setting for motion sensitivity. The shared styles keep pages consistent.
sections.watch_out: Under reduced motion, reveal effects finish almost at once, so content still appears.

sections.name: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)  (part 2)
sections.title: Underline that draws in on hover
sections.what: Adds a thin line under links that slides in from the left on hover or keyboard focus, and stays on the link marked as the current page.
sections.why: Gives links a quiet hover effect that matches the editorial look.
sections.watch_out: The current-page marker depends on the link carrying an aria-current attribute.

sections.name: .grain
sections.title: Faint film grain overlay
sections.what: Lays a very faint static texture over the whole screen. It sits above content but does not block clicks.
sections.why: Adds a subtle printed-film feel. The only stated reason is the comment about digital grain.
sections.watch_out: Even at low opacity it slightly changes every colour on screen, so raising it can hurt readability.

sections.name: .crosshair
sections.title: Crosshair marker container
sections.what: Defines the crosshair as an empty box with no size. The two thin lines that form the cross are drawn from it by the rules below.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets pages drop a crosshair mark into place as decoration.
sections.watch_out: The box has no position setting, so its lines are placed against an outer container and may land in the wrong spot.

sections.name: .crosshair::after
sections.title: Shared style for crosshair lines
sections.what: Gives both crosshair lines their common setup: empty content, absolute placement and a light colour.
sections.why: Keeps the two lines styled the same way.

sections.name: .crosshair::before
sections.title: Horizontal crosshair line
sections.what: Places an 18-pixel-wide, one-pixel-high line so it crosses the centre point.
sections.why: Forms the horizontal half of the cross.

sections.name: .crosshair::after
sections.title: Vertical crosshair line
sections.what: Places an 18-pixel-tall, one-pixel-wide line so it crosses the centre point.
sections.why: Forms the vertical half of the cross.

sections.name: .track-box
sections.title: Tracking frame border
sections.what: Draws a thin, faint border for a tracking frame, which is a box that follows an item on screen. It also hints to the browser that its position and fading will change.
sections.why: Gives a viewfinder feel. Likely reason: the frame is drawn over moving items.
sections.watch_out: The change hint uses extra memory, so apply this class only to frames that actually animate.

sections.name: .track-box::after
sections.title: Shared corner marker for frames
sections.what: Gives the two corner markers on a tracking frame a shared size, a bright outline colour and solid edges.
sections.why: Makes the frame look like a camera viewfinder.

sections.name: .track-box::before
sections.title: Top-left corner marker
sections.what: Places the first corner bracket just outside the top-left of the frame and draws its top and left edges.
sections.why: Completes the viewfinder look at one corner.

sections.name: .track-box::after
sections.title: Bottom-right corner marker
sections.what: Places the second corner bracket just outside the bottom-right of the frame and draws its bottom and right edges.
sections.why: Completes the viewfinder look at the opposite corner.

sections.name: .measure
sections.title: Dashed measuring line
sections.what: Draws a thin dashed horizontal line, like a measuring tape, whose length is meant to be set by script.
sections.why: A decorative measurement mark. The reason is not stated beyond the name.
sections.watch_out: Only the one-pixel height is fixed here, so the width is up to whatever code sets it.

sections.name: .corner-ticks
sections.title: Corner tick marks
sections.what: Adds two short bright ticks, one at the bottom-left and one at the top-right of a box, like crop marks on a printed page.
sections.why: Decorative framing. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Positions are fixed in pixels, so the ticks may not line up if the box changes size a lot.

sections.name: .ruler
sections.title: Ruler with tick marks
sections.what: Draws a thin strip with small ticks every 10 pixels and larger ticks every 50 pixels along the bottom.
sections.why: A decorative ruler that matches the measuring look of the site.

sections.name: .dot-grid
sections.title: Dot grid background
sections.what: Places a faint dot every 24 pixels across an area, like graph paper.
sections.why: Adds a subtle texture. Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .reveal
sections.title: Hidden until revealed on scroll
sections.what: Hides an element and moves it 24 pixels down, ready to fade and rise into place once it is shown.
sections.why: Gives content a gentle entrance as it scrolls into view. The trigger that shows it is not in this file.
sections.watch_out: The element stays invisible until a script adds the is-in class, so a broken trigger hides the content.

sections.name: .reveal.is-in
sections.title: Revealed state
sections.what: When the is-in class is present, the element is fully visible in its normal place.
sections.why: This is the end state of the reveal effect.

sections.name: .draw-line
sections.title: Line hidden before it draws
sections.what: Starts a line at zero width, anchored on the left, ready to be drawn out.
sections.why: Decorative lines that grow into place. Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .draw-line.is-in
sections.title: Line drawn in when revealed
sections.what: Once the is-in class is present on the line or an ancestor, the line grows to its full width.
sections.why: Completes the drawing effect for these lines.

sections.name: .slice-text
sections.title: Headline slice effect base
sections.what: Makes the headline wrapper a box that can hold stacked copies of the text. This supports a hover effect on the contact heading.
sections.why: Lets the heading shift slices of itself on hover, which the comment links to the portrait.

sections.name: .slice-text .slice
sections.title: Overlay copies for slice effect
sections.what: Places the decorative copies of the headline exactly on top of the original, with a smooth 0.55-second movement.
sections.why: The copies have to slide without changing the layout around them.

sections.name: .slice-text .base
sections.title: Original headline kept hidden
sections.what: Hides the original copy but keeps its space, so the layout stays the same while the slices show.
sections.why: Keeps the layout steady while the slice copies move.
sections.watch_out: Only the slice copies show the text, so removing them makes the headline disappear.

sections.name: .slice-text:focus-within .slice
sections.title: Slice shift on hover or focus
sections.what: When the headline is hovered or focused, the slices move sideways by an amount set in a variable named shift.
sections.why: Makes the slice effect respond to both mouse and keyboard.
sections.watch_out: The shift variable must be set on the element, or the slices will not move.

sections.name: .pixel-overlay
sections.title: Full-screen transition layer
sections.what: Lays a full-screen layer above the rest of the page for a pixel-style transition. Clicks pass through it.
sections.why: Likely reason: the transition needs to cover the whole screen. The effect itself is driven elsewhere.
sections.watch_out: The layer sits above the navigation and other layers, so anything placed in it will appear over the page.

sections.name: .thin-scroll
sections.title: Thin scrollbars in panels
sections.what: Makes scrollbars inside panels thin and dark grey so they blend into the design.
sections.why: Keeps panels with long lists tidy. Reason not stated beyond the name.
sections.watch_out: Browser support varies, and some browsers still show their normal scrollbar.

sections.name: .atlas-overlay
sections.title: Atlas label overlay layer
sections.what: Lays a full-size, click-through layer over the 3D view for text labels, in a small uppercase monospace style that fades over 0.6 seconds and clips anything that spills out.
sections.why: Labels sit over the 3D scene without blocking it. The comment calls this the Knowledge Atlas, probably the earlier name for the Memory Palace.
sections.watch_out: Labels that extend past the edges are cut off because overflow is hidden.

sections.name: .atlas-overlay > div
sections.title: Positioned label boxes
sections.what: Makes each direct child box in the overlay sit at the top left, with its position set by script on every frame.
sections.why: Lets labels follow 3D positions cheaply.
sections.watch_out: Labels must be direct children of the overlay for this rule to apply to them.

sections.name: .atlas-clabel
sections.title: Room label base style
sections.what: Sets the base look for room labels in the Atlas: small text, muted colour, one line, no wrapping.
sections.why: Keeps labels readable without crowding the scene.

sections.name: .atlas-clabel span
sections.title: Room label lines stacked
sections.what: Makes each line of a room label its own block, so the code and name sit on separate lines.
sections.why: Separates the code from the name.

sections.name: .atlas-clabel .c-code
sections.title: Dimmed room code
sections.what: Makes the room code quieter than the name beside it.
sections.why: Keeps the name as the main thing to read.

sections.name: .atlas-clabel .c-name
sections.title: Room name size and brightness
sections.what: Sets the room name slightly larger and brighter than the surrounding label text.
sections.why: Makes the name stand out.

sections.name: .atlas-clabel .c-pos
sections.title: Position text hidden by default
sections.what: Hides the position text on each room label until the label is hovered or selected.
sections.why: Keeps labels tidy until someone interacts with them.

sections.name: .atlas-clabel.is-active
sections.title: Brighter room label when active
sections.what: Makes a room label brightest when it is hovered or active.
sections.why: Shows which room is in focus.

sections.name: .atlas-clabel.is-active .c-pos
sections.title: Position text shown when selected
sections.what: Shows the position text at 70 percent strength when the label is hovered or active.
sections.why: Reveals extra detail only for the room in focus.

sections.name: .atlas-clabel.is-dim
sections.title: Faded room label
sections.what: Lowers a room label to 35 percent strength.
sections.why: Likely reason: marks rooms that are not in focus. Reason not stated beyond the class name.

sections.name: .atlas-nlabel
sections.title: Base style for node labels
sections.what: Sets the base look for labels on individual nodes in the Atlas: small, muted, one line, and cut short with dots if too long.
sections.why: Stops long node names from crowding the scene.
sections.watch_out: Names wider than 260 pixels are cut off with dots, so part of the text may not show.

sections.name: .atlas-nlabel .n-code
sections.title: Node code prefix
sections.what: Gives the code at the start of a node label a dimmer colour and extra space after it.
sections.why: Separates the code from the name.

sections.name: .atlas-nlabel.is-related
sections.title: Related node labels brighter
sections.what: Brightens the labels of nodes connected to the selected one.
sections.why: Shows connections at a glance.
sections.watch_out: This only takes effect when script adds the is-related class.

sections.name: .atlas-nlabel.is-strong
sections.title: Strongest node label colour
sections.what: Gives a node label the strongest emphasis, nearly full white.
sections.why: Marks the node that is most in focus.

sections.name: .atlas-bbox
sections.title: Selection box
sections.what: Draws a thin outline box around a selected item. It starts hidden and is shown by script.
sections.why: Highlights the chosen item.

sections.name: .atlas-bbox::after
sections.title: Selection box corner style
sections.what: Gives the two corner brackets on the selection box a shared size and bright outline.
sections.why: Keeps the brackets consistent.

sections.name: .atlas-bbox::before
sections.title: Top-left bracket on selection box
sections.what: Places the top-left corner bracket just outside the box.
sections.why: Frames the selected item at one corner.

sections.name: .atlas-bbox::after
sections.title: Bottom-right bracket on selection box
sections.what: Places the bottom-right corner bracket just outside the box.
sections.why: Frames the selected item at the opposite corner.

sections.name: .atlas-bbox-label
sections.title: Caption above selection box
sections.what: Places a small bright caption just above the selection box, aligned with its left edge.
sections.why: Labels the selected item.
sections.watch_out: The caption sits above its box, so it can be clipped if the box is near the top of its container.

sections.name: .atlas-seltag
sections.title: Small tag hidden by default
sections.what: A small tag with a thin left line, hidden until code shows it.
sections.why: Used to add a short note to a selected item. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: It is hidden by default, so the code must set its display or it will never appear.

sections.name: .atlas-axis
sections.title: Small dim axis label
sections.what: Small, dim text for axis or scale markers. The name suggests this use, but the code that uses it is not in this file.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .label a
sections.title: Buttons and links in labels
sections.what: Buttons and links inside label-styled areas copy the label's capitals and letter spacing so they match. This section also defines the blink animation used by the blinking cursor.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps controls looking like the text around them. The blink keyframes are shared, so they sit here.

sections.name: .cursor-blink
sections.title: Blinking terminal cursor
sections.what: Shows a blinking block cursor, like a terminal, switching on and off once every 1.1 seconds.
sections.why: Adds the terminal feel for nerd mode. The page that uses it places the cursor.
sections.watch_out: Under reduced motion the blink is cut to a single pass, so the cursor may simply stay on.

sections.name: .mode-fade
sections.title: Fade-in when switching modes
sections.what: Fades content in over 0.3 seconds when the display mode changes.
sections.why: Softens the switch between calm and nerd modes.

sections.name: @media (min-width: 1024px)
sections.title: Wide-screen window placement
sections.what: On screens 1024 pixels wide or more, the experience windows take their position, width and offset from per-window CSS variables. Smaller screens keep the default layout.
sections.why: Likely reason: the desktop-style window arrangement needs enough room, so it is limited to wide screens.
sections.watch_out: The positions depend on variables set elsewhere; if those are missing, the windows fall back to defaults.

sections.name: .os-window
sections.title: Experience window opening animation
sections.what: Each experience window opens with a short animation: it fades in and unrolls from the top over about half a second.
sections.why: Likely reason: to make the experience section feel like opening application windows.
sections.watch_out: The animation keyframes named winIn are shared with the tile animation, so changing them changes both.

sections.name: .travel-glitch
sections.title: Contrast boost for travel effect
sections.what: Adds a slight contrast boost to an element while the travel effect is active.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The name suggests a transition effect between sections.

sections.name: .travel-glitch .os-window
sections.title: Dimmed windows during travel
sections.what: While the travel effect is active, experience windows are shown slightly transparent.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .atlas-explabel
sections.title: Atlas explanation label box
sections.what: Styles the explanation label beside a point in the Atlas: small, unwrapped text, a thin left line and a soft fade when it changes.
sections.why: Likely reason: the label must stay readable over the 3D map without taking up much space.
sections.watch_out: Labels do not wrap, so long text can run past the box edge unless child rules cut it short.

sections.name: .atlas-explabel span
sections.title: Each label line on its own row
sections.what: Makes each line inside an Atlas explanation label start on a new row.
sections.why: Likely reason: the label holds a code, a name and details that read best as separate lines.

sections.name: .atlas-explabel .e-code
sections.title: Dim reference code in label
sections.what: Shows the code part of an Atlas label in a faint tone, so it sits behind the name.
sections.why: Likely reason: the code is a reference, not the main message.

sections.name: .atlas-explabel .e-name
sections.title: Main title in Atlas label
sections.what: Sets the name line of an Atlas label in the body font, slightly tighter and larger than other text.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes the name the strongest text in the label.

sections.name: .atlas-explabel .e-meta
sections.title: Truncated detail line in label
sections.what: Shows the detail line of an Atlas label in a dimmer tone, capped at 240 pixels and cut with dots when too long.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the label narrow even when the detail text is long.
sections.watch_out: Long detail text is cut off on screen, so the full text is not visible here.

sections.name: .atlas-explabel.is-strong
sections.title: Highlighted label accent line
sections.what: Brightens the left line of an Atlas label when it is the highlighted one.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows which label is currently selected.

sections.name: .atlas-nlabel.is-dim
sections.title: Faded unrelated node labels
sections.what: Fades node labels to about a third of their strength when they are not the focus.
sections.why: Likely reason: pushes unrelated labels into the background while one is selected.

sections.name: .atlas-year
sections.title: Small year text
sections.what: Shows year text on the Atlas in a small, dim style.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .os-tile
sections.title: Tile opening animation
sections.what: Tiles open with the same unrolling animation as windows, a little faster.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the look consistent across the experience section.
sections.watch_out: Shares the winIn keyframes with the window animation.

sections.name: .atlas-momentsvg
sections.title: Full-size overlay for lines
sections.what: Places an overlay layer over its parent that fills it completely and does not catch mouse clicks.
sections.why: Likely reason: a drawing layer for lines that should not block labels underneath.
sections.watch_out: Because clicks pass through, nothing drawn in this layer can be clicked.

sections.name: .atlas-momentsvg line
sections.title: Faint leader lines
sections.what: Draws the lines in the Atlas overlay as thin, faint blue-white strokes.
sections.why: Likely reason: connects labels to their points without drawing attention.

sections.name: .atlas-momentsvg line.tick
sections.title: Lighter tick lines
sections.what: Draws tick lines in the Atlas overlay even fainter than the main lines.
sections.why: Likely reason: ticks are supporting marks, so they stay quieter.

sections.name: .atlas-tag
sections.title: Atlas tag hidden by default
sections.what: Hides Atlas tags until code shows them, then places them at a point with a glowing shadow for legibility.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the hidden default.
sections.watch_out: A tag stays hidden until another rule or script changes its display; if a tag never shows, check that setting.

sections.name: .atlas-tag::before
sections.title: Blue dot on tags
sections.what: Adds a small glowing blue dot at the left of each Atlas tag.
sections.why: Likely reason: a marker that ties the tag to its point.
sections.watch_out: A later rule changes this dot to amber, and the later rule wins.

sections.name: .atlas-readout
sections.title: Atlas readout panel hidden by default
sections.what: Hides the Atlas readout panel until shown, then gives it a dark translucent box with one line of text and a capped width.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the hidden default and width cap.
sections.watch_out: Text does not wrap, so long readouts are cut at the box edge.

sections.name: .atlas-readout div
sections.title: Cut-off readout rows
sections.what: Cuts each readout row with dots when it is too long for the box.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps every readout row on one line.

sections.name: .atlas-readout span
sections.title: Aligned readout labels
sections.what: Gives the label column in a readout a fixed width and a dimmer tone, so the values line up.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps readout values in a neat column.
sections.watch_out: Labels wider than the fixed column push values out of line.

sections.name: .atlas-momentlabel
sections.title: Moment caption box
sections.what: Styles the caption shown for a moment (a photo in the 3D gallery) as a dark strip with a bottom line, cut with dots when long.
sections.why: Likely reason: captions must read over the photo without covering too much.

sections.name: .hud-scan
sections.title: Scanline and edge shading overlay
sections.what: Adds faint horizontal scanlines and darker edges over a HUD-style panel, for an old-screen look.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. It is decorative, matching the CRT style.

sections.name: .crt::after
sections.title: Flickering CRT screen effect
sections.what: Adds scanlines, darker edges and a slow flicker over the CRT area, using an overlay that does not catch clicks.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives a retro monitor look.
sections.watch_out: The flicker runs forever; it is turned off for visitors who prefer reduced motion.

sections.name: .hud-corner
sections.title: Small corner brackets
sections.what: Draws small thin corner brackets in the paper colour for framing panels.
sections.why: Likely reason: decorative frame corners for HUD panels.

sections.name: .hud-ruler
sections.title: Measuring ruler strip
sections.what: Draws a vertical strip of fine tick marks that fades out toward the right.
sections.why: Likely reason: decorative measuring-scale look.
sections.watch_out: Both the standard and the older browser mask property are set, so keep both when editing.

sections.name: .hud-ruler::after
sections.title: Longer ruler ticks
sections.what: Adds longer tick marks every 50 pixels on top of the ruler strip.
sections.why: Likely reason: marks major divisions on the ruler.

sections.name: .hud-blink
sections.title: Blinking HUD element
sections.what: Makes a HUD element blink slowly.
sections.why: Likely reason: a status indicator effect.
sections.watch_out: Turned off for visitors who prefer reduced motion in a later rule.

sections.name: .hud-panel::before
sections.title: Bright tab on HUD panel
sections.what: Adds a small bright tab on the right edge of a HUD panel.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. It is decorative.

sections.name: .brain-tag
sections.title: Brain map label base style
sections.what: Styles the labels on the hero brain map: hidden by default, placed with transforms, and coloured by a CSS variable named tag, which defaults to cyan.
sections.why: Likely reason: labels follow points on the brain, so they need to be positioned by code.
sections.watch_out: Tags stay hidden until code adds a state class to them.

sections.name: .brain-tag.is-right
sections.title: Orange tag for right hemisphere
sections.what: Switches a brain tag to orange when it belongs to the right side of the map.
sections.why: Likely reason: colour shows which hemisphere a label is from.

sections.name: .brain-tag i
sections.title: Coloured leader line in tag
sections.what: Draws a short glowing line in front of the tag text, in the tag colour.
sections.why: Likely reason: connects the tag text to its point.

sections.name: .brain-tag b
sections.title: Bold heading in brain tag
sections.what: Sets the heading text of a brain tag in bold, small, white type.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .brain-tag em
sections.title: Extra text hidden by default
sections.what: Hides the extra detail text of a brain tag unless the tag is focused.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps tags short until a visitor focuses one.
sections.watch_out: Detail text only appears when the focus state rule applies.

sections.name: .brain-tag.is-named span
sections.title: Named brain tag
sections.what: Shows a name beside the heading of a named brain tag, in the tag colour.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the naming.

sections.name: .brain-tag.is-focus b
sections.title: Larger heading on focus
sections.what: Enlarges the heading of a focused brain tag.
sections.why: Likely reason: emphasises the focused point.

sections.name: .brain-tag.is-focus span
sections.title: Focused tag name style
sections.what: Shows the name in a focused brain tag in the body font, larger and white.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes the focused name the clearest text.

sections.name: .brain-tag.is-focus em
sections.title: Focused tag description
sections.what: Shows the detail text of a focused brain tag as a block, keeping its line breaks, up to 300 pixels wide.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a focused tag show a short description.
sections.watch_out: Line breaks in the source text are kept, so long text shows across several lines.

sections.name: .brain-caption
sections.title: Left hemisphere caption
sections.what: Styles the left-side caption on the brain map: cyan, widely spaced capitals with a soft glow.

summary: The site-wide stylesheet that sets colours, fonts, spacing, motion and decorative effects for every page, including the calm and nerd display modes.
purpose: Defines how the whole site looks and moves, and holds shared styles for text labels, links, the Atlas and vault overlays, and the decorative frames and rulers.
why: Keeps the look in one place so every page shares the same colours and text styles. Reason for the specific grouping is not stated in the code.
how: Step 1 loads the Tailwind styling base. Step 2 defines two colour sets, calm (light and editorial) and nerd (black terminal), chosen by an attribute on the page. Step 3 sets the page background and text colours. Step 4 defines shared text styles and reduces motion for visitors who ask for it. Step 5 defines decorative pieces such as grain, crosshairs, rulers, reveals, and the Atlas and vault overlays.
inputs: A data-mode attribute on the page root chooses calm or nerd. A force-dark class forces the dark colours. Pages use class names such as label, display, rule, reveal and link-quiet. Colours are stored as three plain numbers that other rules read.
outputs: Visual styling only: colours, fonts, spacing, animation and layering across the site.
risks: Colour values use a number format, so a value in the wrong format makes colours disappear. Reduced-motion rules shorten animations across the site. Fonts are named here but must be loaded elsewhere. The file is 812 lines and only the first 59 sections were reviewed for this packet.
debug: If colours look wrong, check the data-mode attribute and the colour values for that mode. If text uses a fallback font, check that the font is loaded in the layout. If content stays invisible, look for the reveal class and whether a script adds the is-in class. If animations seem missing, check the operating system's reduced motion setting. Browser developer tools show which rule applies to an element.

77ea75dd54ae83a8.title: Loads the Tailwind styling base
77ea75dd54ae83a8.what: Pulls in the Tailwind base, component and utility styles. The next colour rule starts here.
77ea75dd54ae83a8.why: Other pages rely on the ready-made classes this brings in.

16f64b3b157232f3.title: Calm light colour set
16f64b3b157232f3.what: Defines the light, quiet colour set used by default, with a near-white background, dark text and grey tones for secondary text and lines. It also sets the body and display fonts and the page side margin.
16f64b3b157232f3.why: Gives the default editorial look. Reason for the exact values is not stated in the code.
16f64b3b157232f3.watch_out: Colour values are plain numbers rather than colour names, so any edit must keep that format.

29281f89733d6e81.title: Dark terminal colour set
29281f89733d6e81.what: Defines the dark, black-terminal colour set used in nerd mode and by any page that forces dark. Its selector list starts on the line before, so it also covers nerd mode.
29281f89733d6e81.why: Gives a second, high-contrast look. Reason for the exact values is not stated in the code.
29281f89733d6e81.watch_out: These values draw text and lines across the site in nerd mode, so a mistake shows up in many places.

651e9be27f956153.title: Nerd mode monospace fonts
651e9be27f956153.what: In nerd mode, switches body and display text to a monospace font, where every letter has the same width, and tightens the letter spacing.
651e9be27f956153.why: Likely reason: matches the black terminal look.
651e9be27f956153.watch_out: The fonts must be loaded by the site, otherwise the browser falls back to a generic monospace font.

f2a54f7cbcc8f333.title: Forced dark background
f2a54f7cbcc8f333.what: Makes any element with the force-dark class show the dark background and light text.
f2a54f7cbcc8f333.why: Lets a page stay dark whichever mode the visitor picked.
f2a54f7cbcc8f333.watch_out: Pages with this class ignore the calm colours, so their text colours must come from the dark set.

1a24e7f0715f985c.title: Page background and text colour
1a24e7f0715f985c.what: Sets the page background and text colour from the current mode, makes jumps to anchors scroll smoothly, and stops phones from resizing text on their own.
1a24e7f0715f985c.why: Keeps the whole page in the chosen mode, including areas outside the main content.
1a24e7f0715f985c.watch_out: Smooth scrolling is switched off for visitors who ask for less motion, so nothing essential should depend on it.

3feddc00500c0dd8.title: Body text and sideways scroll
3feddc00500c0dd8.what: Applies the body font, smooths text rendering, sets background and text colours, fades colour changes over about a third of a second, and hides any sideways overflow.
3feddc00500c0dd8.why: Gives every page one font and a smooth mode switch. Likely reason for hiding overflow: stops layouts sliding sideways on phones.
3feddc00500c0dd8.watch_out: Hiding overflow can silently cut off wide content rather than fixing the layout that made it too wide.

2ccfd6b304608a45.title: Highlight colour for selected text
2ccfd6b304608a45.what: When a visitor selects text, it shows with the paper colour as its background and the ink colour as its letters.
2ccfd6b304608a45.why: Keeps selected text readable in both modes.

eeb8c2540a0bb249.title: Keyboard focus outline
eeb8c2540a0bb249.what: Draws a thin light outline around whatever has keyboard focus, so people using the Tab key can see where they are.
eeb8c2540a0bb249.why: Keyboard users need a visible position on the page.
eeb8c2540a0bb249.watch_out: Removing this rule would make keyboard navigation hard to follow.

8bb8eef1ca412b7e.title: Anchor targets clear the nav bar
8bb8eef1ca412b7e.what: When a link jumps to a section with an id, the page stops that section just below the fixed top bar instead of hiding it underneath.
8bb8eef1ca412b7e.why: The top bar sits over the page, so jumps need extra space.
8bb8eef1ca412b7e.watch_out: The space is based on the nav height value, so change the two together.

42fceccbb4d561cd.title: Reduced motion and shared text styles
42fceccbb4d561cd.what: Turns off most animation and transitions for visitors who ask for less motion. It also defines the shared text styles, such as small monospace labels and large display headings, that pages use.
42fceccbb4d561cd.why: Likely reason: respects a device setting for motion sensitivity. The shared styles keep pages consistent.
42fceccbb4d561cd.watch_out: Under reduced motion, reveal effects finish almost at once, so content still appears.

24a62bd0f87365c1.title: Underline that draws in on hover
24a62bd0f87365c1.what: Adds a thin line under links that slides in from the left on hover or keyboard focus, and stays on the link marked as the current page.
24a62bd0f87365c1.why: Gives links a quiet hover effect that matches the editorial look.
24a62bd0f87365c1.watch_out: The current-page marker depends on the link carrying an aria-current attribute.

4bec854c5c103658.title: Faint film grain overlay
4bec854c5c103658.what: Lays a very faint static texture over the whole screen. It sits above content but does not block clicks.
4bec854c5c103658.why: Adds a subtle printed-film feel. The only stated reason is the comment about digital grain.
4bec854c5c103658.watch_out: Even at low opacity it slightly changes every colour on screen, so raising it can hurt readability.

d6243542d8b5d42a.title: Crosshair marker container
d6243542d8b5d42a.what: Defines the crosshair as an empty box with no size. The two thin lines that form the cross are drawn from it by the rules below.
d6243542d8b5d42a.why: Likely reason: lets pages drop a crosshair mark into place as decoration.
d6243542d8b5d42a.watch_out: The box has no position setting, so its lines are placed against an outer container and may land in the wrong spot.

ab955abe3ddea0a1.title: Shared style for crosshair lines
ab955abe3ddea0a1.what: Gives both crosshair lines their common setup: empty content, absolute placement and a light colour.
ab955abe3ddea0a1.why: Keeps the two lines styled the same way.

b242589f0f344e59.title: Horizontal crosshair line
b242589f0f344e59.what: Places an 18-pixel-wide, one-pixel-high line so it crosses the centre point.
b242589f0f344e59.why: Forms the horizontal half of the cross.

c91c14bfb4f33ed3.title: Vertical crosshair line
c91c14bfb4f33ed3.what: Places an 18-pixel-tall, one-pixel-wide line so it crosses the centre point.
c91c14bfb4f33ed3.why: Forms the vertical half of the cross.

095aa7231620cc21.title: Tracking frame border
095aa7231620cc21.what: Draws a thin, faint border for a tracking frame, which is a box that follows an item on screen. It also hints to the browser that its position and fading will change.
095aa7231620cc21.why: Gives a viewfinder feel. Likely reason: the frame is drawn over moving items.
095aa7231620cc21.watch_out: The change hint uses extra memory, so apply this class only to frames that actually animate.

fdcdaba136f4f575.title: Shared corner marker for frames
fdcdaba136f4f575.what: Gives the two corner markers on a tracking frame a shared size, a bright outline colour and solid edges.
fdcdaba136f4f575.why: Makes the frame look like a camera viewfinder.

0d56a44d3b3b5a79.title: Top-left corner marker
0d56a44d3b3b5a79.what: Places the first corner bracket just outside the top-left of the frame and draws its top and left edges.
0d56a44d3b3b5a79.why: Completes the viewfinder look at one corner.

149540165205c90e.title: Bottom-right corner marker
149540165205c90e.what: Places the second corner bracket just outside the bottom-right of the frame and draws its bottom and right edges.
149540165205c90e.why: Completes the viewfinder look at the opposite corner.

0b684aaff70f3ab3.title: Dashed measuring line
0b684aaff70f3ab3.what: Draws a thin dashed horizontal line, like a measuring tape, whose length is meant to be set by script.
0b684aaff70f3ab3.why: A decorative measurement mark. The reason is not stated beyond the name.
0b684aaff70f3ab3.watch_out: Only the one-pixel height is fixed here, so the width is up to whatever code sets it.

100c4eed55e570ba.title: Corner tick marks
100c4eed55e570ba.what: Adds two short bright ticks, one at the bottom-left and one at the top-right of a box, like crop marks on a printed page.
100c4eed55e570ba.why: Decorative framing. Reason not stated in the code.
100c4eed55e570ba.watch_out: Positions are fixed in pixels, so the ticks may not line up if the box changes size a lot.

0a10ebfc558878e5.title: Ruler with tick marks
0a10ebfc558878e5.what: Draws a thin strip with small ticks every 10 pixels and larger ticks every 50 pixels along the bottom.
0a10ebfc558878e5.why: A decorative ruler that matches the measuring look of the site.

7f692808d3a2babd.title: Dot grid background
7f692808d3a2babd.what: Places a faint dot every 24 pixels across an area, like graph paper.
7f692808d3a2babd.why: Adds a subtle texture. Reason not stated in the code.

72948a211f4f80c5.title: Hidden until revealed on scroll
72948a211f4f80c5.what: Hides an element and moves it 24 pixels down, ready to fade and rise into place once it is shown.
72948a211f4f80c5.why: Gives content a gentle entrance as it scrolls into view. The trigger that shows it is not in this file.
72948a211f4f80c5.watch_out: The element stays invisible until a script adds the is-in class, so a broken trigger hides the content.

318a749a72fe2dcd.title: Revealed state
318a749a72fe2dcd.what: When the is-in class is present, the element is fully visible in its normal place.
318a749a72fe2dcd.why: This is the end state of the reveal effect.

cb4d8ff94910fdd9.title: Line hidden before it draws
cb4d8ff94910fdd9.what: Starts a line at zero width, anchored on the left, ready to be drawn out.
cb4d8ff94910fdd9.why: Decorative lines that grow into place. Reason not stated in the code.

006c12af01c59cc3.title: Line drawn in when revealed
006c12af01c59cc3.what: Once the is-in class is present on the line or an ancestor, the line grows to its full width.
006c12af01c59cc3.why: Completes the drawing effect for these lines.

fc329b6b91e33b70.title: Headline slice effect base
fc329b6b91e33b70.what: Makes the headline wrapper a box that can hold stacked copies of the text. This supports a hover effect on the contact heading.
fc329b6b91e33b70.why: Lets the heading shift slices of itself on hover, which the comment links to the portrait.

85667200c0936c3b.title: Overlay copies for slice effect
85667200c0936c3b.what: Places the decorative copies of the headline exactly on top of the original, with a smooth 0.55-second movement.
85667200c0936c3b.why: The copies have to slide without changing the layout around them.

7e66a403d4fd6efd.title: Original headline kept hidden
7e66a403d4fd6efd.what: Hides the original copy but keeps its space, so the layout stays the same while the slices show.
7e66a403d4fd6efd.why: Keeps the layout steady while the slice copies move.
7e66a403d4fd6efd.watch_out: Only the slice copies show the text, so removing them makes the headline disappear.

2e2a94339df40008.title: Slice shift on hover or focus
2e2a94339df40008.what: When the headline is hovered or focused, the slices move sideways by an amount set in a variable named shift.
2e2a94339df40008.why: Makes the slice effect respond to both mouse and keyboard.
2e2a94339df40008.watch_out: The shift variable must be set on the element, or the slices will not move.

1c940c25dc286e72.title: Full-screen transition layer
1c940c25dc286e72.what: Lays a full-screen layer above the rest of the page for a pixel-style transition. Clicks pass through it.
1c940c25dc286e72.why: Likely reason: the transition needs to cover the whole screen. The effect itself is driven elsewhere.
1c940c25dc286e72.watch_out: The layer sits above the navigation and other layers, so anything placed in it will appear over the page.

fb2c59bd0c8e06c4.title: Thin scrollbars in panels
fb2c59bd0c8e06c4.what: Makes scrollbars inside panels thin and dark grey so they blend into the design.
fb2c59bd0c8e06c4.why: Keeps panels with long lists tidy. Reason not stated beyond the name.
fb2c59bd0c8e06c4.watch_out: Browser support varies, and some browsers still show their normal scrollbar.

b2b3a596b1dc27f6.title: Atlas label overlay layer
b2b3a596b1dc27f6.what: Lays a full-size, click-through layer over the 3D view for text labels, in a small uppercase monospace style that fades over 0.6 seconds and clips anything that spills out.
b2b3a596b1dc27f6.why: Labels sit over the 3D scene without blocking it. The comment calls this the Knowledge Atlas, probably the earlier name for the Memory Palace.
b2b3a596b1dc27f6.watch_out: Labels that extend past the edges are cut off because overflow is hidden.

9b1617b537c9073d.title: Positioned label boxes
9b1617b537c9073d.what: Makes each direct child box in the overlay sit at the top left, with its position set by script on every frame.
9b1617b537c9073d.watch_out: Labels must be direct children of the overlay for this rule to apply to them.

002bc71a6127d836.title: Room label base style
002bc71a6127d836.what: Sets the base look for room labels in the Atlas: small text, muted colour, one line, no wrapping.
002bc71a6127d836.why: Keeps labels readable without crowding the scene.

1ad7a1f5608bf305.title: Room label lines stacked
1ad7a1f5608bf305.what: Makes each line of a room label its own block, so the code and name sit on separate lines.
1ad7a1f5608bf305.why: Separates the code from the name.

a500e32b93d48fe9.title: Dimmed room code
a500e32b93d48fe9.what: Makes the room code quieter than the name beside it.
a500e32b93d48fe9.why: Keeps the name as the main thing to read.

a2c69275d58cd1da.title: Room name size and brightness
a2c69275d58cd1da.what: Sets the room name slightly larger and brighter than the surrounding label text.

8f5b8c30bc674ae8.title: Position text hidden by default
8f5b8c30bc674ae8.what: Hides the position text on each room label until the label is hovered or selected.
8f5b8c30bc674ae8.why: Keeps labels tidy until someone interacts with them.

d5086f989b329cef.title: Brighter room label when active
d5086f989b329cef.what: Makes a room label brightest when it is hovered or active.
d5086f989b329cef.why: Shows which room is in focus.

ea76913c072ff615.title: Position text shown when selected
ea76913c072ff615.what: Shows the position text at 70 percent strength when the label is hovered or active.
ea76913c072ff615.why: Reveals extra detail only for the room in focus.

aef91c48899561d0.title: Faded room label
aef91c48899561d0.what: Lowers a room label to 35 percent strength.
aef91c48899561d0.why: Likely reason: marks rooms that are not in focus. Reason not stated beyond the class name.

f906a7933302f739.title: Base style for node labels
f906a7933302f739.what: Sets the base look for labels on individual nodes in the Atlas: small, muted, one line, and cut short with dots if too long.
f906a7933302f739.why: Stops long node names from crowding the scene.
f906a7933302f739.watch_out: Names wider than 260 pixels are cut off with dots, so part of the text may not show.

09b7ba3c04dd04b3.title: Node code prefix
09b7ba3c04dd04b3.what: Gives the code at the start of a node label a dimmer colour and extra space after it.
09b7ba3c04dd04b3.why: Separates the code from the name.

487eedd451bafd58.title: Related node labels brighter
487eedd451bafd58.what: Brightens the labels of nodes connected to the selected one.
487eedd451bafd58.watch_out: This only takes effect when script adds the is-related class.

2be1f91873c32a3c.title: Strongest node label colour
2be1f91873c32a3c.what: Gives a node label the strongest emphasis, nearly full white.
2be1f91873c32a3c.why: Marks the node that is most in focus.

816a03798bce8adc.title: Selection box
816a03798bce8adc.what: Draws a thin outline box around a selected item. It starts hidden and is shown by script.

444653d8a33119e0.title: Selection box corner style
444653d8a33119e0.what: Gives the two corner brackets on the selection box a shared size and bright outline.

3f2ba97343f52cbf.title: Top-left bracket on selection box
3f2ba97343f52cbf.what: Places the top-left corner bracket just outside the box.
3f2ba97343f52cbf.why: Frames the selected item at one corner.

a031abf4d45be80c.title: Bottom-right bracket on selection box
a031abf4d45be80c.what: Places the bottom-right corner bracket just outside the box.
a031abf4d45be80c.why: Frames the selected item at the opposite corner.

33f7703afc8cbb06.title: Caption above selection box
33f7703afc8cbb06.what: Places a small bright caption just above the selection box, aligned with its left edge.
33f7703afc8cbb06.watch_out: The caption sits above its box, so it can be clipped if the box is near the top of its container.

7b5a8387bd1e388f.title: Small tag hidden by default
7b5a8387bd1e388f.what: A small tag with a thin left line, hidden until code shows it.
7b5a8387bd1e388f.why: Used to add a short note to a selected item. Reason not stated in the code.
7b5a8387bd1e388f.watch_out: It is hidden by default, so the code must set its display or it will never appear.

efeab2c3290bd9ef.title: Small dim axis label
efeab2c3290bd9ef.what: Small, dim text for axis or scale markers. The name suggests this use, but the code that uses it is not in this file.
efeab2c3290bd9ef.why: Reason not stated in the code.

b847f18a045916ec.title: Buttons and links in labels
b847f18a045916ec.what: Buttons and links inside label-styled areas copy the label's capitals and letter spacing so they match. This section also defines the blink animation used by the blinking cursor.
b847f18a045916ec.why: Likely reason: keeps controls looking like the text around them. The blink keyframes are shared, so they sit here.

70a25bf849cd5f89.title: Blinking terminal cursor
70a25bf849cd5f89.what: Shows a blinking block cursor, like a terminal, switching on and off once every 1.1 seconds.
70a25bf849cd5f89.why: Adds the terminal feel for nerd mode. The page that uses it places the cursor.
70a25bf849cd5f89.watch_out: Under reduced motion the blink is cut to a single pass, so the cursor may simply stay on.

3ec230941c1f1580.title: Fade-in when switching modes
3ec230941c1f1580.what: Fades content in over 0.3 seconds when the display mode changes.
3ec230941c1f1580.why: Softens the switch between calm and nerd modes.

e2a541633d25925a.title: Wide-screen window placement
e2a541633d25925a.what: On screens 1024 pixels wide or more, the experience windows take their position, width and offset from per-window CSS variables. Smaller screens keep the default layout.
e2a541633d25925a.why: Likely reason: the desktop-style window arrangement needs enough room, so it is limited to wide screens.
e2a541633d25925a.watch_out: The positions depend on variables set elsewhere; if those are missing, the windows fall back to defaults.

d9b8855eb78452f3.title: Experience window opening animation
d9b8855eb78452f3.what: Each experience window opens with a short animation: it fades in and unrolls from the top over about half a second.
d9b8855eb78452f3.why: Likely reason: to make the experience section feel like opening application windows.
d9b8855eb78452f3.watch_out: The animation keyframes named winIn are shared with the tile animation, so changing them changes both.

b07fc5c3f5520b2a.title: Contrast boost for travel effect
b07fc5c3f5520b2a.what: Adds a slight contrast boost to an element while the travel effect is active.
b07fc5c3f5520b2a.why: Reason not stated in the code. The name suggests a transition effect between sections.

c1c55b0f4a3a050a.title: Dimmed windows during travel
c1c55b0f4a3a050a.what: While the travel effect is active, experience windows are shown slightly transparent.
c1c55b0f4a3a050a.why: Reason not stated in the code.

6c9041d75aaff3c9.title: Atlas explanation label box
6c9041d75aaff3c9.what: Styles the explanation label beside a point in the Atlas: small, unwrapped text, a thin left line and a soft fade when it changes.
6c9041d75aaff3c9.why: Likely reason: the label must stay readable over the 3D map without taking up much space.
6c9041d75aaff3c9.watch_out: Labels do not wrap, so long text can run past the box edge unless child rules cut it short.

fcfa4dccb871428d.title: Each label line on its own row
fcfa4dccb871428d.what: Makes each line inside an Atlas explanation label start on a new row.
fcfa4dccb871428d.why: Likely reason: the label holds a code, a name and details that read best as separate lines.

36fa9fe1dd885d36.title: Dim reference code in label
36fa9fe1dd885d36.what: Shows the code part of an Atlas label in a faint tone, so it sits behind the name.
36fa9fe1dd885d36.why: Likely reason: the code is a reference, not the main message.

5f5de8780e5cb30b.title: Main title in Atlas label
5f5de8780e5cb30b.what: Sets the name line of an Atlas label in the body font, slightly tighter and larger than other text.
5f5de8780e5cb30b.why: Likely reason: makes the name the strongest text in the label.

099603fc6f83acbd.title: Truncated detail line in label
099603fc6f83acbd.what: Shows the detail line of an Atlas label in a dimmer tone, capped at 240 pixels and cut with dots when too long.
099603fc6f83acbd.why: Likely reason: keeps the label narrow even when the detail text is long.
099603fc6f83acbd.watch_out: Long detail text is cut off on screen, so the full text is not visible here.

89c27f11dd10d9db.title: Highlighted label accent line
89c27f11dd10d9db.what: Brightens the left line of an Atlas label when it is the highlighted one.
89c27f11dd10d9db.why: Likely reason: shows which label is currently selected.

b74f10535301c5eb.title: Faded unrelated node labels
b74f10535301c5eb.what: Fades node labels to about a third of their strength when they are not the focus.
b74f10535301c5eb.why: Likely reason: pushes unrelated labels into the background while one is selected.

5b3f31094f469ae6.title: Small year text
5b3f31094f469ae6.what: Shows year text on the Atlas in a small, dim style.
5b3f31094f469ae6.why: Reason not stated in the code.

3c4f1f0fc17185aa.title: Tile opening animation
3c4f1f0fc17185aa.what: Tiles open with the same unrolling animation as windows, a little faster.
3c4f1f0fc17185aa.why: Likely reason: keeps the look consistent across the experience section.
3c4f1f0fc17185aa.watch_out: Shares the winIn keyframes with the window animation.

88fbb813fd2e2a83.title: Full-size overlay for lines
88fbb813fd2e2a83.what: Places an overlay layer over its parent that fills it completely and does not catch mouse clicks.
88fbb813fd2e2a83.why: Likely reason: a drawing layer for lines that should not block labels underneath.
88fbb813fd2e2a83.watch_out: Because clicks pass through, nothing drawn in this layer can be clicked.

c9e347b066422c4e.title: Faint leader lines
c9e347b066422c4e.what: Draws the lines in the Atlas overlay as thin, faint blue-white strokes.
c9e347b066422c4e.why: Likely reason: connects labels to their points without drawing attention.

bad7c9fd6b7a212d.title: Lighter tick lines
bad7c9fd6b7a212d.what: Draws tick lines in the Atlas overlay even fainter than the main lines.
bad7c9fd6b7a212d.why: Likely reason: ticks are supporting marks, so they stay quieter.

4fd2375879e01190.title: Atlas tag hidden by default
4fd2375879e01190.what: Hides Atlas tags until code shows them, then places them at a point with a glowing shadow for legibility.
4fd2375879e01190.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the hidden default.
4fd2375879e01190.watch_out: A tag stays hidden until another rule or script changes its display; if a tag never shows, check that setting.

e9123d777cd6b031.title: Blue dot on tags
e9123d777cd6b031.what: Adds a small glowing blue dot at the left of each Atlas tag.
e9123d777cd6b031.why: Likely reason: a marker that ties the tag to its point.
e9123d777cd6b031.watch_out: A later rule changes this dot to amber, and the later rule wins.

19e93d31dffe79dc.title: Atlas readout panel hidden by default
19e93d31dffe79dc.what: Hides the Atlas readout panel until shown, then gives it a dark translucent box with one line of text and a capped width.
19e93d31dffe79dc.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the hidden default and width cap.
19e93d31dffe79dc.watch_out: Text does not wrap, so long readouts are cut at the box edge.

babb158ee2638fe1.title: Cut-off readout rows
babb158ee2638fe1.what: Cuts each readout row with dots when it is too long for the box.
babb158ee2638fe1.why: Likely reason: keeps every readout row on one line.

4cef37117f549b41.title: Aligned readout labels
4cef37117f549b41.what: Gives the label column in a readout a fixed width and a dimmer tone, so the values line up.
4cef37117f549b41.why: Likely reason: keeps readout values in a neat column.
4cef37117f549b41.watch_out: Labels wider than the fixed column push values out of line.

5d3be1de43978db8.title: Moment caption box
5d3be1de43978db8.what: Styles the caption shown for a moment (a photo in the 3D gallery) as a dark strip with a bottom line, cut with dots when long.
5d3be1de43978db8.why: Likely reason: captions must read over the photo without covering too much.

0d1cf2cd256f8384.title: Scanline and edge shading overlay
0d1cf2cd256f8384.what: Adds faint horizontal scanlines and darker edges over a HUD-style panel, for an old-screen look.
0d1cf2cd256f8384.why: Reason not stated in the code. It is decorative, matching the CRT style.

a53cb6f71e6aec8f.title: Flickering CRT screen effect
a53cb6f71e6aec8f.what: Adds scanlines, darker edges and a slow flicker over the CRT area, using an overlay that does not catch clicks.
a53cb6f71e6aec8f.why: Likely reason: gives a retro monitor look.
a53cb6f71e6aec8f.watch_out: The flicker runs forever; it is turned off for visitors who prefer reduced motion.

bd5741bf33554ea9.title: Small corner brackets
bd5741bf33554ea9.what: Draws small thin corner brackets in the paper colour for framing panels.
bd5741bf33554ea9.why: Likely reason: decorative frame corners for HUD panels.

37af0efcefa2875c.title: Measuring ruler strip
37af0efcefa2875c.what: Draws a vertical strip of fine tick marks that fades out toward the right.
37af0efcefa2875c.watch_out: Both the standard and the older browser mask property are set, so keep both when editing.

b826e2007a7f8039.title: Longer ruler ticks
b826e2007a7f8039.what: Adds longer tick marks every 50 pixels on top of the ruler strip.
b826e2007a7f8039.why: Likely reason: marks major divisions on the ruler.

577ca09d70b6731e.title: Blinking HUD element
577ca09d70b6731e.what: Makes a HUD element blink slowly.
577ca09d70b6731e.why: Likely reason: a status indicator effect.
577ca09d70b6731e.watch_out: Turned off for visitors who prefer reduced motion in a later rule.

f2d90f13ad5c6f8c.title: Bright tab on HUD panel
f2d90f13ad5c6f8c.what: Adds a small bright tab on the right edge of a HUD panel.
f2d90f13ad5c6f8c.why: Reason not stated in the code. It is decorative.

074df6ecf2a4481b.title: Brain map label base style
074df6ecf2a4481b.what: Styles the labels on the hero brain map: hidden by default, placed with transforms, and coloured by a CSS variable named tag, which defaults to cyan.
074df6ecf2a4481b.why: Likely reason: labels follow points on the brain, so they need to be positioned by code.
074df6ecf2a4481b.watch_out: Tags stay hidden until code adds a state class to them.

2b1508629716d273.title: Orange tag for right hemisphere
2b1508629716d273.what: Switches a brain tag to orange when it belongs to the right side of the map.
2b1508629716d273.why: Likely reason: colour shows which hemisphere a label is from.

856f52c8bf30a4b3.title: Coloured leader line in tag
856f52c8bf30a4b3.what: Draws a short glowing line in front of the tag text, in the tag colour.
856f52c8bf30a4b3.why: Likely reason: connects the tag text to its point.

f7b42a07f25eaee4.title: Bold heading in brain tag
f7b42a07f25eaee4.what: Sets the heading text of a brain tag in bold, small, white type.
f7b42a07f25eaee4.why: Reason not stated in the code.

db6d499692af0941.title: Extra text hidden by default
db6d499692af0941.what: Hides the extra detail text of a brain tag unless the tag is focused.
db6d499692af0941.why: Likely reason: keeps tags short until a visitor focuses one.
db6d499692af0941.watch_out: Detail text only appears when the focus state rule applies.

b4e4247de62a036c.title: Named brain tag
b4e4247de62a036c.what: Shows a name beside the heading of a named brain tag, in the tag colour.
b4e4247de62a036c.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the naming.

fd40a5ac84f55d2e.title: Larger heading on focus
fd40a5ac84f55d2e.what: Enlarges the heading of a focused brain tag.
fd40a5ac84f55d2e.why: Likely reason: emphasises the focused point.

b6f05fe8bde06594.title: Focused tag name style
b6f05fe8bde06594.what: Shows the name in a focused brain tag in the body font, larger and white.
b6f05fe8bde06594.why: Likely reason: makes the focused name the clearest text.

eaca4e4239ad54ad.title: Focused tag description
eaca4e4239ad54ad.what: Shows the detail text of a focused brain tag as a block, keeping its line breaks, up to 300 pixels wide.
eaca4e4239ad54ad.why: Likely reason: lets a focused tag show a short description.
eaca4e4239ad54ad.watch_out: Line breaks in the source text are kept, so long text shows across several lines.

9546a2f4698e8e9e.title: Left hemisphere caption
9546a2f4698e8e9e.what: Styles the left-side caption on the brain map: cyan, widely spaced capitals with a soft glow.
9546a2f4698e8e9e.why: Likely reason: matches the cyan colour of left-side labels.

22c82d191130b68b.title: Right hemisphere caption
22c82d191130b68b.what: Makes the right-side caption orange, matching the right-side labels.
22c82d191130b68b.why: Likely reason: colour matches the hemisphere.

2fd3234e90ac0bcf.title: Name tag frame
2fd3234e90ac0bcf.what: Draws a thin pale border with a soft glow and a dark translucent background around a name tag.
2fd3234e90ac0bcf.why: Reason not stated in the code. It is decorative.

a3ccb3f7ead85fd1.title: Name tag colour wash
a3ccb3f7ead85fd1.what: Lays a coloured gradient over the name tag image using a colour blend mode.
a3ccb3f7ead85fd1.why: Likely reason: tints the photo to match the site palette.
a3ccb3f7ead85fd1.watch_out: Colour blend modes can look different across browsers, so check the result in more than one.

90ec24f6852a5b92.title: Reduced motion switch-off
90ec24f6852a5b92.what: Turns off the CRT flicker and the HUD blink animations for visitors who prefer reduced motion.
90ec24f6852a5b92.why: Likely reason: some visitors are bothered or unwell from motion, so the site respects their setting.
90ec24f6852a5b92.watch_out: Any new looping animation on these classes needs its own entry here.

d5ec9a0d54463b86.title: Vault graph label base
d5ec9a0d54463b86.what: Hides vault graph labels until shown, positions them absolutely and keeps them on one line.
d5ec9a0d54463b86.why: Likely reason: labels are placed by code and shown only when needed.
d5ec9a0d54463b86.watch_out: The same selector is defined again later; the later white-space setting wins.

3512c053d7ef3240.title: Vault label text style
3512c053d7ef3240.what: Sets vault labels in small, spaced, uppercase, dim text.
3512c053d7ef3240.why: Reason not stated in the code. It is a quiet label style.

ab8be91942e19a3a.title: Dim code in vault label
ab8be91942e19a3a.what: Makes the code part of a vault label dim and not bold.
ab8be91942e19a3a.why: Likely reason: the code is secondary to the label name.

1ca016fa043dc127.title: Vault label span colour
1ca016fa043dc127.what: Makes spans inside a vault label inherit the label colour.
1ca016fa043dc127.why: Reason not stated in the code. It keeps colours consistent.

7f77cad9c875cbd7.title: Hide extra label text on small screens
7f77cad9c875cbd7.what: Hides the extra spans in vault labels on screens 760 pixels wide or less.
7f77cad9c875cbd7.why: Likely reason: narrow screens have no room for the extra text.
7f77cad9c875cbd7.watch_out: Anything placed in these spans disappears on phones, so do not put essential information there.

fed39a90be283b50.title: Active vault label
fed39a90be283b50.what: Brightens a vault label when it is the active one.
fed39a90be283b50.why: Likely reason: shows which item is selected.

2de023fce38e344d.title: Active label code block
2de023fce38e344d.what: Shows the code of an active vault label as an inverted block, with paper background and dark text.
2de023fce38e344d.why: Likely reason: makes the active code stand out.

ec8bf9821405232c.title: Vault section heading
ec8bf9821405232c.what: Styles small spaced section headings in the vault graph, brighter than labels.
ec8bf9821405232c.why: Reason not stated in the code. It marks groups of nodes.

f22aa4842e23a8e7.title: Vault graph node text
f22aa4842e23a8e7.what: Sets vault graph node text to a small size with wrapping allowed and a bright tone.
f22aa4842e23a8e7.why: Likely reason: nodes hold short descriptions that may need several lines.
f22aa4842e23a8e7.watch_out: This second definition of the same selector overrides the earlier no-wrap setting.

e59563b4505bd5ec.title: Dim code in vault node
e59563b4505bd5ec.what: Makes the code part of a vault node dim.
e59563b4505bd5ec.why: Likely reason: the code is secondary to the node text.

15a85c4ccaae8fd7.title: Vault room backdrop and shared label rule
15a85c4ccaae8fd7.what: Sets the vault room background to a dark warm brown gradient, then starts a shared selector list for Atlas labels and tags.
15a85c4ccaae8fd7.why: The header comment says palace labels sit on solid boxes so they read over the point cloud.
15a85c4ccaae8fd7.watch_out: The selector list continues into the next section, so adding a label type means editing that section too.

df457b9fddb5655d.title: Solid box for Atlas labels
df457b9fddb5655d.what: Gives every label in the shared list a solid dark box with a thin amber border and no text shadow.
df457b9fddb5655d.why: The header comment says labels sit on solid boxes so they stay readable over the point cloud.
df457b9fddb5655d.watch_out: This body applies to all labels in the list, not only tags.

7cc387b66c438731.title: Room for the Atlas tag dot
7cc387b66c438731.what: Adds extra left padding to Atlas tags so the dot has room.
7cc387b66c438731.why: Likely reason: makes space for the dot drawn at the left.
7cc387b66c438731.watch_out: This overrides the earlier left padding for the same selector.

bb23da3b71bef9e8.title: Bright Atlas node labels
bb23da3b71bef9e8.what: Sets Atlas node labels to a bright, mostly opaque paper colour.
bb23da3b71bef9e8.why: Likely reason: node labels must be readable on the dark background.

318b82b8cbaf8b97.title: Amber dot on Atlas tags
318b82b8cbaf8b97.what: Moves the Atlas tag dot to the middle left and colours it amber with a soft glow, replacing the earlier blue dot.
318b82b8cbaf8b97.why: Likely reason: amber matches the other Atlas tag borders.
318b82b8cbaf8b97.watch_out: The later definition overrides the earlier blue dot for the same element.
